newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crude prices rise in Asia, light wet crudes strong.
newsitem.headline: Crude prices rise in Asia, light wet crudes strong.

text.p: Crude oil futures were higher during Asian business hours on Wednesday, while trading in January light crude grades from the Gulf kicked off to a brisk start, buoyed by firm buying interest, traders said.

Market participants said there were few fresh incentives, particularly as the API had decided to postpone the release of its weekly data until 4.30 p.m. EST (2130 GMT) on Wednesday. The delay, of one day, was due to insufficient information as a result of the Veteran's Day holiday on Monday.
December cash Brent was notionally assessed at $22.95/23.00.

At 0815 GMT, December Brent was most recently traded at $22.93 on SIMEX compared with the IPE settlement of $22.83 on Tuesday. Brent/Dubai spreads were around levels similar to late U.S. trading. January Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $1.92/1.97, while February was notionally assessed at $1.87/1.92.

In the wet market, a European major sold a 500,000-barrel January Qatar Land at a premium of 45 cents above the official selling price. The buyer is believed to be a Japanese refiner. Two 450,000-barrel January Qatar Land cargoes are also believed to have exchanged hands.

One barrel was sold by a trading company at 43 cents and the other -- believed done most recently by the major -- at 53 cents. There were few, if any, cargoes of January Qatar Land left, traders said.

Traders said January Murban, another light Gulf crude, was also likely to sell briskly. One cargo holder said the offer was for 60 cents above the official selling price. There were unlikely to be buyers at a premium of 50 cents, he said.
An Odudu for December 1-10 lifting was believed to have been sold to a South Korean refiner at dated Brent plus 30 cents. -- M.Yoshikawa/Tokyo +81-3-5473-3706
